name: Tip of the Tongue Phenomenon
description: A person can feel sure they know a word or name yet be temporarily unable to retrieve it. During the state, partial information often remains available, such as the first letter, syllable pattern, or semantically related alternatives.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to search, autocomplete, contact lookup, command palettes, naming systems, and recovery aids for known-but-not-fully-recalled information. It matters most where users know what they want but cannot produce the exact string unaided.
prevalence_note: Very familiar in everyday language and psychology, and useful in search/retrieval design discussions, but not commonly taught as a standalone canonical UX heuristic.

findings.description: Brown's review concludes that tip-of-the-tongue states are a nearly universal retrieval phenomenon, often especially tied to proper names, with reliable partial access to target-word features and resolution during the episode about half the time.
findings.source_title: A review of the tip-of-the-tongue experience.
